sections.overview: The Greater Painted-snipe is a secretive wetland bird with a broad range across Africa and Asia.
sections.identification: The female is larger and more brightly coloured than the male, an unusual reversal of the usual pattern.
sections.habitat: It favors shallow wetlands with dense vegetation, including marshes and flooded grassland.
sections.diet: It is omnivorous, taking insects and other small invertebrates as well as seeds.
sections.behavior: The female courts several males; males undertake incubation and care for the chicks.
sections.reproduction: The nest is a shallow cup on the ground among vegetation near water.
sections.ecology: It is generally resident, though some populations make short movements as wetland conditions change.
sections.conservation: BirdLife’s global assessment lists it as Least Concern, while noting a decreasing population trend.
